title: Key expression evaluates safely
statement: Let a counting-sort input have $n$ items stored at source address $s$, with key values $k_i$ satisfying $0\le k_i<N$. Assume the word and address bounds and the disjointness conditions required for the counting-sort layout hold, and that the initial memory contains item $i$ at $s+i$ and key $k_i$ at its designated key cell. If a modified memory agrees with the initial memory outside the destination and counter ranges, then, for every $i<n$ and all integers $c,p$, the key-loading expression is safe in the state with loop variables $i,c,p$ and modified memory, and evaluates to $k_i$.
hypotheses_covered: Counting-sort preconditions: word bound, source/destination/counter bounds, item and key contents, key range, and required interval disjointness
Modified memory agrees with initial memory outside destination and counter ranges
caveat: The statement depends on a large bundled precondition and a specific key-loading expression whose full definition is not present in the given definitions.
